name: T-GADE
one_liner: An LLM evolution framework that picks survivors by minimizing a 'free energy' so a temperature setting trades off quality against diversity.

loop.proposes: Structured artifacts (here, bin packing scoring heuristics) from LLM crossover, mutation and a self-repair step
loop.judged_by: Evaluation on online bin packing, measured as excess bins over the volume lower bound
loop.steers: Survival selection minimizes free energy F_T = <E> - T*H, with temperature T controlling the quality-diversity balance

headline_result: In a preregistered seed-paired comparison at 400 total LLM calls on online bin packing, the HoxLM configuration won 9 of 10 runs against EoH, with a median sealed excess of 0.836% against 3.912%.
caveat: Preprint (arXiv v2, 14 Oct 2026), one task, 10 seed pairs, and an EoH-aligned implementation. Not independently replicated.
beyond_harness_note: A physics-inspired selection rule over a population steers the search, and the evolved scoring rules are readable and run without the model.
generative_model: Pretrained LLM, frozen (also used as a self-repair model, HoxLM)
algorithmic_authority: Bin packing evaluation and free-energy survival selection

sources.title: T-GADE: Thermodynamical Generative-AI-Driven Evolution of LLM Artifacts

verification.notes: Resolved arXiv:2609.12286 (Ogawa and Mori; v1 10 Sep 2026, v2 14 Oct 2026). Abstract numbers match the draft's direction (better sample efficiency than EoH at equal calls); added the exact 9/10 and 0.836% vs 3.912% figures. The draft's 'preprint' label confirmed. Affiliations not checked, so org lists the authors. Parent left null: the paper says its example is aligned with EoH but frames T-GADE as a general framework. Org confirmed from the arXiv HTML title block: Graduate School of Informatics, Osaka Metropolitan University (review 2026-11-03).
